The rolling experiment was designed with three rolling reductions, namely 20%, 50%, and 80%, and the samples corresponding to these reductions were designated as Alloy-20, Alloy-50, and Alloy-80, respectively.

The Nb35Zr26Ti19Hf15Mo5 (atomic percent, at.%) alloy was prepared by vacuum levitation melting using a water-cooled copper crucible in the smelting equipment SMTX-XF-10 (SUMMIT NEW MATERIALS). The furnace vacuum degree was 3 × 10−3 Pa, and high-purity argon gas was used for protection. The process of repeated remelting was carried out 5–6 times to ensure the homogeneity of the ingot.

The multi-pass rolling method was adopted to roll in the lengthwise direction. The original thickness of the rolled sample is 10 mm. The rolling process is carried out along the length direction. The linear velocity of the rolling mill rolls is 600 mm/s, and the reduction per pass is 0.1 mm. The rolling experiment was designed with three rolling reductions, namely 20%, 50%, and 80%, and the samples corresponding to these reductions were designated as Alloy-20, Alloy-50, and Alloy-80, respectively.

From the XRD diffraction pattern, it can be seen that the Nb35Zr26Ti19Hf15Mo5 alloy consists of a single-phase BCC solid solution, and there is no ordered peak at the low-angle diffraction position.
After etching, a typical dendritic and interdendritic structure was observed.
